text.p: Bonds eased but with no great selling pressure as a predicted technical correction took place.

The easier tone to the longer-dated bonds steepened the yield curve slightly but without any easing of yields at the shorter end. "It is a very technical market. There is some profit-taking at the longer end but the range of prices should be pretty narrow," said one trader.
"There is not much selling pressure in the 10-years but the spread could widen slightly with the Bund," added another trader. "But there should be support at 68 basis points," he said.

The market was trading at a spread of 65, unchanged on Friday. Traders said that there was little in the way of news with the G7 meeting over the weekend having produced little for the markets to react to.
They said that the shorter end was gaining some support from hopes that the Bank of Spain will cut the repo rate on Tuesday.
But it would be risky to bet on the Bank of Portugal following suit even if Spain does move, they added.
